# Atlas Mind

> A self-hostable, git-native knowledge base and an AI memory over MCP. Your notes stay plain Markdown files in your own private git repository, served by a single Python standard-library server — no database, your content sent nowhere. AGPL-3.0.

Atlas Mind is a self-hosted wiki / knowledge-base engine and an external brain you share with your AI over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It is a Notion / Obsidian-Publish alternative built on three ideas: own the data (plain files in your own git repo), own the engine (a small Python server you can read line by line), and own the mind (an AI memory you can read and edit by hand, not an opaque vector store). If the engine vanished, your mind still opens in any text editor.

## Key pages
- [Homepage](https://atlas-mind.anakior.app/): what Atlas Mind is — the problem (rented minds), the three pillars, and the MCP "superpowers".
- [Live demo](https://atlas-mind.anakior.app/demo/): the real viewer running entirely in your browser (offline build) — browse the guides and features, the force-directed Mind graph, and the activity layer. No signup.

## Project
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Anakior/atlas-mind): source (Python, standard library only), install and self-hosting documentation, AGPL-3.0.
- [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/atlas-mind/): install with `uv tool install atlas-mind` or `pipx install atlas-mind`, then `atlas serve ~/my-mind`.
- [MCP server](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/): published as `app.anakior/atlas-mind`: 30 tools to read, write, triage, map, rewind and audit a knowledge base over MCP.

## What it does
- Multi-format: Markdown is first-class (rendered, linked, searched); standalone HTML decks, PDF, Word `.docx`, images and JSON are previewed inline, rendered in the browser.
- AI-native: an MCP endpoint exposes 30 tools across six groups: read, write (with backlink fixups), graph traversal, time-travel over git history, an activity/attribution layer (who changed what, AI-authored detection, stale docs, same-topic contradictions), and an inbox that agents stage ready-to-file items into for you to triage. It is a persistent, local, read-and-write memory for an AI.
- Built for agents: a one-call topic brief within a token budget, search hits that carry how far to trust them (last editor, AI or human, stale, contradicted), edits returned as diffs with dry runs and a concurrent-change guard, a cursor to catch up on what changed, and an agent's whole work session undoable as one commit. Assistants connect over OAuth 2.1 (sign-in with 2FA, a consent screen to narrow what they get, revocable); tokens can also be minted by hand and limited to read, inbox and/or write; the mind's AGENTS.md is sent to every MCP client as its instructions. Prompts the person starts by name: built-ins (weekly review, contradiction triage, new document from a template) and their own, written as Markdown in the mind. Every document is an MCP resource (doc://<path>) a client can attach. Speaks MCP 2026-07-28 (stateless) and the earlier revisions.
- Lightweight and self-contained: one Python HTTP server on the standard library, no database (accounts and share links are plain JSON on disk), vendored fonts and libraries; your content is never sent anywhere — the only outbound request by default reads an MCP client's public metadata when you connect it over OAuth (switchable off).
- Collaboration: per-document access control in cloud mode, plus a pull-based "Hive Mind" that mirrors a slice of another instance's content as read-only nodes.
